reader.requirement: At --std 85 a period followed by a space (or a line end, or the end of the source) is the separator period, which ends a sentence or stands where a format shows it (after headers, paragraph-names, entries, END PROGRAM); a separator period anywhere else, a period with no space after it, and a format's required period left out must be refused, while a period inside a PICTURE character-string or numeric literal is a symbol, not a separator.
reader.edition-search: Read SeparatorRule.cs whole (DOT arm, IsSeparatorSpace treats end of text as a separator) and PictureSeparatorPeriodRule.cs; grepped Edition|Version|Std in both (none); Frontend.cs#LexAndParse runs both over the token stream with no edition argument. The grammar's DOT placements are shared by every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: w73a_separator_context_conforming covers sentence-ending periods; the negative w73a-period-not-followed-by-space covers the missing space; nothing covers a misplaced separator period, an omitted required period, the end-of-source period or PICTURE-final insertion periods

reader.notes: The lexer makes every period not taken by a literal or PICTURE a DOT; SeparatorRule refuses one with no space after it, and the grammar places DOT only where the formats show it, so a misplaced separator period is a parse error. The diagnostics cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85, a message-text matter only.
